children: I brought in wearables—Garmin, Strava—to passively capture sleep, heart rate variability, and daily rhythm. Over time, patterns emerged. Bipolar shifts weren’t random—they followed circadian drift. Actigraphy gave me the missing layer: foresight. Paired with AI, I began building visual timelines that aligned physical, cognitive, and emotional states. This allowed for predictive logic—seeing destabilisation before it struck. Where medication had failed to prevent episodes, data offered clarity.

As a researcher or healthcare professional, utilizing actigraphy data becomes instrumental in unraveling the complex dynamics of these interconnected aspects. Actigraphy, a non-invasive method of monitoring sleep-wake cycles, provides a wealth of information that extends beyond merely tracking sleep duration. In this context, my motivation to leverage actigraphy data stems from a profound desire to gain deep insights into mood patterns.
